summary: A 1933 log-and-frame L-5 cabin on Burton Peak in Boundary County, abandoned in 1967, still standing and reached by a hike of about 2.5 miles.

facts.design: Log and frame 14 by 14 foot cabin, the Nez Perce L-5 design; the register calls it the only remaining L-5 log frame lookout house in North Idaho
facts.status_note: Abandoned since 1967; the cabin stands but is showing its age, and volunteers have made emergency repairs

access.note: A hike-in on Kaniksu National Forest land, described as a popular destination hike. The cabin is abandoned and not in service. No source read says whether going inside is allowed.

visit.trail_note: Hike of about 2.5 miles one way with 1,500 feet of gain from the end of Forest Road 2411 at the trailhead (WillhiteWeb). Inland NW Routes gives 5.2 miles round trip, moderate. Snow at the trailhead at the end of FR 2411 may last until late spring.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m 4.3 is not supported by any page read; it matches the 14-foot footprint, so a correction proposes removing it. Elevation (6,844 ft, 2,086 m) and the 1933 build and 1967 abandonment agree across sources. Staff names come from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; Idaho Fire Lookouts adds Larry Johnson (1935) and Mr. Malcom Smith (1945), which firelookout.com does not list. Spelling of the design name differs ('Nez Perce' on firelookout.com, 'Nez Pierce' on WillhiteWeb). The Idaho Fire Lookouts page includes reader comments, which are not cited. Access and trail details come from a hiking guide and a personal site and are dated 2021 to 2023, so check current road and trailhead conditions before publishing. Photo credits (Tyler Nyman, Carol Elam collection) have no image URLs, so no photo entries were added.
